did_you_know.text: In this verse, Moses shapes the tablets while God writes on them. This differs from the first tablets, which Scripture also describes as the work of God.
Verses 6–7 are traditionally called the “Thirteen Attributes of Mercy.” The number thirteen comes from a traditional way of dividing the phrases.
In the ancient world, a treaty with another people could be both a political and a religious alliance. The Torah therefore warns that such an agreement could influence Israel’s faith.
The Hebrew word for “cast image” is connected with pouring metal into a mold. It refers to an image made by human hands, not only to a stone statue.
“The month of Aviv” is a seasonal name for the month of Passover, when the grain begins to ripen. In a later period, this month was called Nisan.
The donkey is the only animal specifically mentioned here whose firstborn is redeemed with a lamb. If it was not redeemed, it had to be killed because it could not be offered as a sacrifice.
Sabbath rest is required during both plowing and harvest, two especially busy seasons for farmers. This emphasizes that rest does not depend on having an easy time for work.

Shavuot and Sukkot are described here in agricultural terms: Shavuot is linked with the wheat harvest, and Sukkot with the ingathering. Later traditions also gave these festivals major historical meanings.
The three yearly journeys are the basis of the idea of the “three pilgrimage festivals”: Passover, Shavuot, and Sukkot. During the Temple period, they involved traveling to the central sanctuary.
The prohibition against cooking a kid in its mother’s milk appears three times in the Torah. It became a foundation for separating meat and milk in Jewish law.

The Hebrew word can be connected both with horns and with radiating light. An ancient Latin translation understood the verse as describing a horned face, influencing artworks such as Michelangelo’s statue of Moses.
The rare Hebrew word masveh appears only in this chapter, three times. Here it means a covering or veil placed over Moses’ face.
